issue: isRevisionRangeToken reads any token with '..' between two non-dot, non-slash characters as a git revision range, so a file-list review target whose path holds '..' inside a name (for example docs/notes..v2.md) is routed to scopeInsideTouchedFiles. With no reviewScopeFiles on record that path returns true, so the review-target relevance check admits every scope (fail-open) instead of narrowing to the named file. Reach is narrow: an operator-supplied file target with a double-dot file name. Hardening only, since no caller is known to send one. A fix could require the range's two sides to have no '/' or file extension, or fall back to path containment when reviewScopeFiles is empty.

issue: deriveDimension now walks the configured custom dimension names (buildDimensionUniverse) with a bare substring test over free text (iteration focus + finding title + description). A short custom name the config contract allows, such as 'ui' or 'api', matches inside unrelated words ('build', 'guide', 'rapid'), so when no canonical dimension name appears a finding is labelled with the custom dimension instead of falling back to iteration.dimensionsAddressed[0]. Before this change only the four canonical names were tested, so no custom name could mislabel a finding. Case: reviewDimensions ['correctness','ui'], a finding titled 'build step skips lint' in an iteration whose focus names no canonical dimension, gets dimension 'ui'. Inferred from reading the code; no command reproduced it.

writeLineageFrontierStore writes frontier-nodes.jsonl first and uses its existence as the 'already seeded' marker, then appends the research inbox in a second call. If the inbox append throws (ENOSPC, EACCES) or the process dies between the two writes, the next spawn attempt sees the store, returns false, and never writes the inbox. The research lineage then runs with no seeded inbox rows for its dealt frontier nodes, and nothing repairs that. The store write is also a plain writeFileSync rather than an atomic write. Reach: only an I/O failure or a kill between two synchronous writes, so this is hardening, not a correctness blocker.

issue: The Completed Runs section and the Upgrade Notes (line 249) say --extend=N takes N more iterations, but leave out the catch that README.md line 143, quick-reference.md and loop-protocol.md all state: an extension keeps the run's stop policy, so under stopPolicy convergence an extension with nothing new can stop again at its first convergence check. A reader who follows the Upgrade step on a run created with the default convergence settings gets no new passes. The changelog template says every problem a reader could run into is named. Line 166 says the policy is kept but never says what that means for the reader.

The Upgrade line tells readers to add a custom name to review_dimensions, but does not say custom dimensions apply to single-executor runs only. A fan-out run binds review_dimensions: all in every lineage (runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs lines 1796 and 1895, and before this change as well), so a fan-out user's custom name is silently ignored. README.md line 45, the feature catalog and the command presentation all state this limit. The release entry does not.

A behavior change that hits default runs is in no changelog. The review graph upsert now adds one FINDING node and one EVIDENCE_FOR edge for each finding that has a path:line ref (deriveReviewFindingEvidence). It also folds prefixed leaf finding ids onto the stored node (resolveReviewFindingId). For every loop type, an edge to an undeclared node is now skipped and listed in rejectedOrphanEdges, where the whole batch used to roll back. Commit 7c6a2d9a7e5 says 'This changes default runs': before it, a review graph whose leaf sent no evidence edges could never allow a stop. None of hub v2.1.0.0-v2.1.7.0, runtime v1.10.0.0, deep-review v1.11.18.0/v1.12.0.0/v1.13.0.0 or deep-research v1.16.0.0 mentions it. Only runtime/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md:620 describes it.
